extracted.intended_audience: science teachers, textbook authors, and readers of Nature (scientists and educators)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative guidance used by reviewers to judge scientific and technical books (especially physics/mechanics textbooks and engineering/technical monographs), focusing on suitability for target students, pedagogical clarity, technical accuracy, and usefulness for teaching and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for intended audience and level
rubrics_metrics.description: Books should be written specially to suit the varied conditions under which teachers and pupils work (elementary school, high school, public school, technical school, college, cramming schools, artisans in evening schools, matriculated students, pass-degree students, matriculation pupils).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the book is 'not too difficult for young students, but which contains all that is really essential' (No. 1); whether it 'is intended for artisans in evening schools' (No. 2); whether a work 'is only a school book... containing all of the subject that is required for the London University Matriculation' but may be 'too thorough' for some examinations (No. 7); and whether a volume 'is a complete elementary manual' for matriculated students (No. 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and logical order of experimental instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of experiments should be clear and the order of experiments logical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise given when 'the instructions given seem to be very clear in the main, and the order of experiment is quite logical' (No. 1). Criticism where students are not told 'what they are expected to see or what conclusions they should draw' (No. 2) or where experiment descriptions are inadequately connected to theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate balance between experiment and theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether theoretical exposition should accompany experiments or be left to the teacher; preface experiments with short theoretical accounts where helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author's opinion noted that theory 'should be given by the teacher — at any rate in the first year' (No. 1). Praised when 'Each experiment is prefaced by a short theoretical account' adding value (No. 3); criticized when experimental courses are 'wholly experimental' without guiding what to observe (No. 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and inclusion of essential material
rubrics_metrics.description: Text should include all that is really essential for its intended course or examination level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'first course' should 'contain all that is really essential' (No. 1). 'Properties of Matter' intended to include 'all that is usually required for a pass degree' and thus deserves strict examination (No. 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with examination syllabuses and curricula
rubrics_metrics.description: Where intended for examination preparation, the text should match the syllabus requirements and provide material needed for revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'This book... supply a want, viz. a work containing approximately all that is required by the syllabuses in experimental science set for the Oxford and Cambridge junior local and Central Welsh Board junior examinations' (No. 3). Evaluate whether subject-matter covers required topics and whether conditions of producing the book preclude originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical aids and exercise grading
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide well-graded exercises, end-of-chapter questions, hints, and graduated papers suitable for the student age and level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise for 'a set of questions' at chapter ends (No. 3) and 'an abundance of well graduated exercises suitable for boys of twelve to thirteen years old' (Young). Hints on solving riders and graduation by difficulty are considered useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practicality and cost considerations for experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments should be arranged to keep cost low where appropriate and distinguish between those meant for properly equipped laboratories and those possible at home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commended when 'the latter have been arranged so as to keep the cost of performance low' while avoiding 'merely trifling experiments' (No. 6). Note which experiments are 'meant to be done in a laboratory, if not at home.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and currency of technical units and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Text should use up-to-date units, reference current standards, and avoid obsolete measures or assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticised for using 'Borda's metre' and 'Borda's kilogram' which 'has long been obsolete' and for apparent ignorance of 'the work of the Bureau International' (No. 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of conceptual errors and misleading phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid imprecise or incorrect statements (e.g., confusion of weight and mass; improper definitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of poor phrasing: calling 'a strong push to displace appreciably a large ball of iron... indicates its great weight, and not its great mass' — reviewers correct mass/weight confusion (No. 4). Regret at phrase 'whole pressure' defined incorrectly (No. 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical consistency and connection between definitions and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions introduced (e.g., force defined as rate of change of momentum) should be connected to how the term is used throughout the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticized when 'Force is defined in the introduction as rate of change of momentum; no attempt is made to connect this definition with the use of the word force in the body of the book' (No. 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and relevance of illustrations and diagrams
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations must be numerous, accurate, and directly useful to the point under discussion; poor or misleading diagrams are detrimental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise when 'profusely illustrated with sketches, which will prove of great use to teachers who are obliged to make their own apparatus' (No. 6) or where photographs 'will do much to make the non-technical reader familiar' (Biles). Criticism when familiar 'lines-of-force' diagrams misrepresent reality or a frontispiece is 'somewhat superfluous' (Nos. 7 and 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and vitality of treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Text should show originality in treatment to make reading interesting and stimulate teachers and students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praised 'originality of treatment which makes it interesting reading' (No. 7) and the attempt to 'introduce vitality into his subject' (No. 5). Acknowledge limitations where examination-style textbooks may 'preclude originality' (No. 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and treatment of problems (for problem collections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems should be well-chosen, of practical interest, and where appropriate include worked solutions or answers in a considered balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commended 'selection of problems has been very well made' and 'novelty about the choice of problems' (No. 8). Recommend 'more of these problems were worked out in detail' and note the 'middle ground' of giving answers to about half the questions; order and arrangement of questions should be logical ('work, force, motion' criticized) (No. 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate level of mathematical rigor and proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide proofs and mathematical quotations at a level appropriate to the intended students while acknowledging when some material is likely beyond them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valued when 'a proof is given of most of the theorems, stated, and this is usually sufficient for those who intend to proceed only to a pass degree' (No. 5). Note that 'matriculation pupil will not understand the mathematical quotations... but these quotations will serve to keep many a teacher on the right path' (No. 7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and correctness of physical models and assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure models (e.g., rolling friction, representation of waves) are physically reasonable and do not involve implicit fallacies (e.g., perpetual motion in a model).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticized that the usual solution for a disc rolling down an inclined plane 'involves perpetual motion' if friction is represented improperly; suggestion to include ideas of rolling friction (No. 5). Debate over representing waves by wave-fronts versus rays is framed as a question of convenience but correctness when deviation from sphericity matters (Millikan & Gale).

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness of photographic and experimental documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For technical monographs and experimental claims, photographic evidence, photographs of apparatus and worked calculations increase the book's utility and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise for 'well illustrated' reproductions of photographs of turbine construction and for 'calculations, necessary in determining blade dimensions... being fully worked out' (Biles). In letters, experimental claims are evaluated by whether sterilisation and photographic procedures are adequate and whether organisms were photographed 'almost as soon as they were found'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarising and applying experimental results
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should summarise trustworthy experimental information and show how to apply results (e.g., experiments at US Navy Tank, graphs applied to propeller design).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commended when experiments are 'admirably summarised; the results are illustrated by graphs, and their application to the design of a propeller... is clearly explained' (Biles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate structure, order and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The sequence of topics, chapters and exercises should follow a pedagogically sensible order; odd or counterintuitive ordering is criticized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questioned the order of questions in Sanborn's book ('work, force, motion' — 'Is it possible that it is intended that the exercises should be performed backwards?') (No. 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of superfluous or distracting material
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations or frontispieces that do not contribute to understanding should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frontispiece of an engine 'belching black smoke' described as 'somewhat superfluous' and misleading due to wrong perspective (No. 8); include illustrations only when they 'illustrate a definite point.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of reproducibility and experimental rigor in controversial claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For experimental discoveries or claims (e.g., origin-of-life experiments), adequacy of sterilisation, prevention of contamination, timely photographic documentation, and the possibility of independent replication are criteria for evaluating validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a letter defending experimental claims, author insists sterilisation 'is fully shown in the book', organisms were received 'on a sterilised slip' and 'photographed almost as soon as they were found'; notes that disbelief may stem from unwillingness to attempt replication ('we regard archebiosis as so great a miracle that we do not expect to see it repeated').
